title: IB API maturity
claim: Interactive Brokers provides mature flexible API for high-speed data and execution with wide instrument access and low commissions
support: Author compares IB favorably vs Fidelity, TD Ameritrade, E*Trade, LightSpeed on API design and fees
mechanism: Non-blocking callback model, contract/order field flexibility
validation: Validate against current IB fee schedule

title: TWS API EClient-EWrapper pattern
claim: TWS API uses EClient (requests) and EWrapper (callbacks) in multithreaded architecture for request-response
support: Author explains request-response pattern with void request functions and callbacks
mechanism: Multithreaded: main thread sends requests, decoder processes responses
validation: Connect to TWS and observe request-response flow

title: Contract fundamental fields
claim: Minimal contract requires symbol, secType, currency, and exchange; example IBM: symbol=IBM, secType=STK, currency=USD, exchange=SMART
support: Author provides Python code snippet for IBM stock contract
mechanism: IB validates contract against security database
validation: Create contracts for multiple instruments

title: Order transmit field
claim: Order.transmit=False prevents execution until manually enabled; used in bracket orders
support: Bracket order example shows parent and first child with transmit=False, last child with transmit=True
mechanism: IB checks transmit flag before routing to execution
validation: Submit orders with transmit True and False

title: Bracket orders: parent-child structure
claim: Bracket order combines main order with child stop order and child limit order, linked via parentId; children inactive until parent fills
support: Complete code example shows main BUY, SELL STP at lower price, SELL LMT at higher price
mechanism: Parent execution triggers child activation; only one profit target executes
validation: Submit bracket order and monitor all three fills

title: Stop order adjustment: one-time modification
claim: IB allows one modification to stop orders via child order with triggerPrice and adjustedStopPrice
support: Example shows adjusting stop from 75 to 85 when price crosses 90
mechanism: IB maintains adjustment state; modification applies once; requires parentId linking
validation: Submit adjustable stop and trigger adjustment via price movement

title: Order execution algorithms: TWAP, VWAP, etc.
claim: IB supports six order submission algorithms: adaptive, percentage of volume, arrival price, dark ice, TWAP, VWAP to break large orders into slices
support: Author lists six algorithms for breaking large orders to minimize market impact
mechanism: Algorithm selects slice size and timing based on market conditions
validation: Must consult current IB documentation for algorithm parameters

title: Financial data access: technical, fundamental, news
claim: IB provides real-time and historical technical data (bars at multiple timeframes), tick data, fundamental company data, and news feeds
support: Chapter covers technical data access, fundamental data queries, news subscriptions
mechanism: IB data infrastructure feeds real-time data to clients; historical data queried on demand
validation: Subscribe to feeds and validate against exchange or primary sources

title: Execution safety: transmit=False until validation
claim: Production systems should set transmit=False initially and verify order fields before transmit=True to prevent accidental large orders
support: Author's bracket order pattern uses transmit=False to batch-verify before execution
mechanism: Transmit field acts as safety gate; verified orders only execute when True
validation: Code review: verify transmit=False until validation complete

title: Connection error recovery in multithreaded API
claim: TWS API client must handle connection loss, reconnection, and thread synchronization between main and callback threads
support: Author warns application may hang/disconnect if steps out of order; references multithreading complexity
mechanism: API spawns background threads; main thread can block if callbacks stall
validation: Connection fault injection tests; verify recovery within SLA

title: Commission structure impacts algorithm profitability
claim: IB commissions (significantly lower than competitors) directly reduce algorithm net alpha; lower commission improves small-edge strategy viability
support: Author lists low commissions as reason for choosing IB; implicit in profitability analysis
mechanism: Commission reduces net proceeds of each trade
validation: Validate all backtests with current IB commissions; ensure realistic execution cost assumptions

title: Order lifecycle: submission to fill to settlement
claim: Order lifecycle: created -> submitted -> accepted -> routed -> filled -> confirmed -> settled; system must track state at each stage
support: Author discusses order data retrieval and implicit state model in callbacks
mechanism: IB updates order status via callbacks as state changes
validation: Monitor order callbacks and compare state transitions to IB documentation

title: Order ID collision risk in high-throughput systems
claim: Systems placing many orders rapidly must manage order IDs to avoid collisions; IB requires unique orderId per session
support: Author shows bracket order example with manual orderId assignment (mainId, mainId+1, mainId+2); implicit assumption of safe ID allocation
mechanism: IB rejects duplicate orderId; missed ID can cause order submission to fail silently
validation: Load test: verify no ID collisions under high order rate; monitor IB rejection messages

title: Block and scale orders: breaking large orders
claim: IB supports block orders (automatic splitting) and scale orders (custom division) to minimize market impact of large orders
support: Author lists block and scale orders as capabilities for large volumes
mechanism: IB splits orders into market-friendly slices
validation: Requires current IB documentation on block/scale order parameters

title: Historical data: bars and ticks
claim: IB provides historical bar data at multiple timeframes and tick-level data for backtesting and research
support: Author covers reqHistoricalData and bar formats; ticks retrievable for analysis
mechanism: IB historical database indexed by symbol, secType, timeframe
validation: Validate historical prices against exchange or Yahoo Finance

title: Account types: cash and margin
claim: IB account types (cash, margin) determine leverage availability; margin rules and interest rates apply to margin accounts
support: Author discusses account setup and fees in section 1.1.2
mechanism: Account type controls buying power and margin requirements
validation: Compare IB margin terms to current website and confirm with account manager

title: Bollinger-MFI: mean reversion strategy
claim: Bollinger Bands + Money Flow Index (MFI) system detects overbought/oversold conditions; entry when price touches band and MFI confirms
support: Author combines Bollinger Bands with MFI for mean-reversion signals; tests on historical data
mechanism: Bands define overbought/oversold; MFI filters false signals; mean reversion assumption
validation: Backtest Bollinger-MFI system 2020-present; compare walk-forward performance to 2019 results

title: Turtle Trading System: trend-following with ATR
claim: Entry on 20-day highest price, stop loss at 2*ATR below entry, exit when trend reverses; trend-following system adapts to volatility
support: Author describes system entry (20-day high), stop (ATR multiple), and trend logic with worked example
mechanism: ATR captures volatility; trailing stop adapts to market regime
validation: Backtest Turtle system 2020-present; compare to 2019 baseline results

title: Candidate selection strategy: multi-stage filtering
claim: SimpleAlgo uses sentiment (investor state), technical filters (volume, price patterns), and thresholds to narrow candidate pool before signal application
support: Author describes candidate selection pipeline: sentiment evaluation -> candidate list -> technical confirmation
mechanism: Funnel reduces computational cost and false signal rate
validation: Ablation study: remove each filter stage and measure impact on signal quality

title: SimpleAlgo: sentiment-driven candidate selection and execution
claim: End-to-end algo system: evaluate investor sentiment, screen candidate stocks, apply breakout signal, place orders via TWS API
support: Chapter 14 presents SimpleAlgo implementation with sentiment analysis, filtering, and breakout strategy
mechanism: Sentiment-driven candidate list feeds to signal generator; signal threshold triggers order submission
validation: Backtest SimpleAlgo logic against historical breakout signals; compare to random entry baseline
